To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
most of the changes in smoking behaviour and exposure that occurred on switching to cigarettes with reduced tar and nicotine yields persisted over a long time period.

most effects of switching from high to low yield cigarettes persist for at least six months, suggesting that the current strategy of reducing exposure by lowering tar and/or nicotine yields may be ineffective.
switching to lower tar and nicotine yield cigarettes does not lead to a reduction in exposure to smoke constituents, as measured by cotinine levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the long-term effects of smoking low tar and nicotine yield cigarettes, and the implications for the control of smoking.
the long-term effects of switching cigarette brands.
the effects on smokers of switching to cigarettes of lower tar and nicotine yield, and in particular with the long-term effects of switching.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of smoking cigarettes with lower tar yields are complex and variable, and that there are few, if any, long term health benefits.
the long-term effects of switching cigarettes to lower tar and nicotine are minimal and of no clinical significance.
the effects of smoking cigarettes with lower nicotine and tar yields are not sustained.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of switching to low yield cigarettes are not sustained.
smokers who switch to cigarettes with lower nicotine yields smoke more intensely and are exposed to more smoke.
switching from high yield cigarettes to low yield cigarettes does not result in a significant reduction in exposure to the toxic constituents of cigarette smoke.
The main takeaway from our work is that

smokers are not passive consumers of cigarettes, but rather active participants in their own addiction, and that they are capable of modifying their behaviour in ways that can offset the beneficial effects of reduced tar and nicotine yields.
smokers who switch from one brand of cigarettes to another with lower nicotine yields do not necessarily reduce their exposure to nicotine.
switching to lower yield tobacco products is unlikely to be effective for reducing exposure to tobacco smoke.
